status.en: 11 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Mogadishu, Baidoa and Jameeco.
status.nb: 11 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Mogadishu, Baidoa og Jameeco.

summary.en: Somalia's Supreme Court rejected President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term extension, prompting armed forces to seize the court and threats to the chief's life. Security forces opened fire on protesters in Mogadishu, killing at least three civilians in clashes over home demolitions and two others in separate police shootings. Government troops were attacked near Leego town and Somali soldiers were left unburied after a deadly al-Shabaab clash, while the police deputy chief warned of a security vacuum as Ugandan troops withdraw. The conflict caused 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Somalias høyesterett avviste president Hassan Sheikh Mohamuds forlengelse av mandatet, noe som førte til at væpnede styrker tok kontroll over retten og truet sjefens liv. Sikkerhetsstyrker skjøt mot demonstranter i Mogadishu, og drepte minst tre sivile i sammenstøt om husnedrivninger, samt to andre i separate politiskudd. Regjeringssoldater ble angrepet nær byen Leego, og somaliske soldater ble liggende ubegravd etter en dødelig al-Shabaab-kamp, mens politiets nestleder advarte om et sikkerhetsvakuum når ugandiske tropper trekker seg tilbake. Konflikten forårsaket 2 284 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Somali Civil War (2009–present)
background.extract: The ongoing phase of the Somali Civil War began in 2009 and is concentrated in southern and central Somalia, primarily between the forces of the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS), assisted by African Union peacekeeping forces, and the Islamist militant group al-Shabaab, which pledged allegiance to al-Qaeda in 2012.
